name: Erta Ale
notes: Persistent lava lake in summit caldera, one of the world's few long-lived lava lakes.

name: Nyiragongo
notes: Lava lake active in the summit crater since at least 1971; fissure eruption reached Goma in May 2021.

name: Nyamuragira
notes: Africa's most active volcano, with frequent effusive basaltic eruptions from summit and flank vents.

name: Piton de la Fournaise
notes: One of the world's most frequently active basaltic shield volcanoes, erupting roughly every 1-2 years.

name: Ol Doinyo Lengai
notes: Only volcano known to erupt natrocarbonatite lava, an unusually low-temperature magma.

name: Mount Michael
notes: Persistent lava lake confirmed via satellite thermal imagery, near-continuous eruption since November 2014.

name: Heard Island (Big Ben)
notes: Remote, glacier-covered stratovolcano; active summit vent is Mawson Peak.

name: Erebus
notes: One of the few volcanoes on Earth with a persistent lava lake, active since at least 1972.

name: Stromboli
notes: Essentially continuous mild Strombolian explosions recorded for over a millennium.

name: Etna
notes: Europe's most active volcano, with frequent summit and flank eruptions.

name: Kilauea
notes: Persistent and recurring lava lake activity at Halemaumau crater within Kilauea caldera.

name: Kilauea Lower East Rift Zone (2018)
notes: 2018 lower East Rift Zone eruption near Fissure 8 fed a lava channel to Kapoho Bay; distinct site about 14 km ESE of the Kilauea summit.

name: Mauna Loa
notes: Erupted from its Northeast Rift Zone November-December 2022, its first eruption since 1984.

name: Ambrym
notes: Active lava lakes historically maintained within the Marum and Benbow pit craters.

name: Yasur
notes: Essentially continuous Strombolian/Vulcanian activity since at least 1774.

name: Manam
notes: Frequently active island stratovolcano 13 km off PNG's north coast.

name: Bagana
notes: Persistently active, with viscous andesitic lava dome and flow effusion.

name: Nishinoshima
notes: Island substantially enlarged by effusive and explosive activity across 2013-2023.

name: Sakurajima (Aira caldera)
notes: Post-caldera cone of Aira caldera; frequent explosions and ash plumes at Minamidake crater.

name: Krakatau (Anak Krakatau)
notes: 2018 flank collapse triggered a deadly tsunami; the cone has rebuilt with frequent eruptions since.

name: Dukono
notes: Near-continuous ash and thermal emission since 1933, one of the longest-running eruptions on record.

name: Ibu
notes: Persistently active since 1998 lava dome growth began, with frequent explosions.

name: Semeru
notes: Frequently active, with pyroclastic flows down the Besuk Kobokan drainage on the SE flank.

name: Merapi
notes: Persistent lava dome growth and collapse generates frequent pyroclastic flows.

name: Bardarbunga (Holuhraun 2014-15)
notes: Holuhraun fissure eruption, August 2014-February 2015, produced Iceland's largest lava flow since 1783; site about 18 km NE of Bardarbunga's own caldera.

name: Fagradalsfjall
notes: First Reykjanes Peninsula eruption in about 800 years; effusive fissure activity in nearby Geldingadalir, March-September 2021.

name: Litli-Hrutur / Sundhnukur
notes: Sundhnukur crater row erupted repeatedly December 2023-2025 near Grindavik; preceded by the Litli-Hrutur fissure, July-August 2023.

name: Cumbre Vieja (Tajogaite 2021)
notes: Longest historical eruption on La Palma, September-December 2021, with an extensive lava flow field to the coast.

name: Villarrica
notes: Persistently active basaltic-andesite stratovolcano with an intermittently active summit lava lake.

name: Sierra Negra
notes: Largest caldera in the Galapagos; June-August 2018 fissure eruption produced lava flows covering over 30 sq km.

name: Wolf
notes: Erupted in 2015 and again January-April 2022, with an SO2 plume and southeast-flank lava flows.

name: Fernandina
notes: Most frequently active Galapagos shield volcano; March 2024 eruption was its largest in 15 years.

name: Fuego
notes: Near-daily Strombolian explosions, with occasional pyroclastic and lava flows.

name: Pacaya
notes: Persistent lava flow and Strombolian activity from Mackenney crater, continuously since 1961.

name: Masaya
notes: Santiago crater hosts a small persistent lava lake with ongoing degassing since October 2015.

name: Sangay
notes: Ecuador's most active volcano, with frequent daily explosions and ash-gas plumes.

name: Reventador
notes: Most frequently active of Ecuador's eastern-cordillera volcanoes, with recurring lava flows.

name: Popocatepetl
notes: Current eruptive period began January 2005 and continues, with frequent gas-ash exhalations.

name: Tolbachik (2012-2013 Fissure Eruption)
notes: November 2012-September 2013 fissure eruption from vents about 6-7 km south of the Plosky Tolbachik summit produced Kamchatka's largest basaltic lava flow field in decades.

name: Klyuchevskoy
notes: Highest and most active volcano on Kamchatka, with near-continuous explosive and effusive activity.

name: Shiveluch
notes: Persistent lava dome growth with frequent pyroclastic flows and ash emissions.
